page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.sn2ne family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports several advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation (AVX-512F), AES cryptography, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. These hardware-level features assist with vector calculations and cryptographic tasks, although the overall performance is constrained by the dual-vCPU configuration.

Across standardized benchmarks, the ecs.sn2ne.large demonstrates entry-level performance profiles. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 1442.69. Memory bandwidth tests show similar limitations, with uncached read and write speeds of 10.65 GB/sec and 9.53 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench and Passmark scores consistently rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the older generation of the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest processing power, this instance is best suited for lightweight, steady-state workloads that require predictable CPU access without high compute demands. Suitable applications include basic static web serving, small-scale database operations, and low-throughput Redis caching. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-cost entry point for legacy x86_64 applications, though its low benchmark-per-resource ratio makes it less optimal for modern, compute-intensive tasks.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results place this instance in the lower performance tiers, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and memory bandwidth metrics consistently ranking in the bottom 10% to 25%. Consequently, the ecs.sn2ne.large is best suited for lightweight, steady-state workloads such as basic static web serving, small database operations, and low-throughput caching where dedicated CPU allocation is required but raw processing power is not a priority.
